title: Action level disagrees between summary table and detail page
detail: The Failure Code Table and the code's own troubleshooting page state different action levels for the same code.
impact: Action level drives whether the machine may keep working. L01 and L04 are not interchangeable. The assistant must not silently pick one.

title: Cross-references to codes that do not exist in this manual
detail: A troubleshooting procedure tells the technician to go and troubleshoot another failure code, but that code has no page and is not in the summary table.
impact: These are dead ends. Several of the referenced codes belong to other machine models or to superseded manual revisions.

title: Codes whose entire procedure is a redirect
detail: The complete troubleshooting content is a single instruction to go and troubleshoot a different code.
impact: This is the classic RAG trap. Retrieval returns a technically correct, perfectly relevant chunk that gives the technician nothing to do. Hop-expansion is mandatory, not an optimisation.

title: Codes with no parsable troubleshooting steps
detail: The page exists but its layout matches neither of the two table formats used elsewhere in Section 40.
impact: Requires manual transcription or a vision pass. Excluded from step-based evaluation until then.

title: Steps whose number is rendered inside the cause column
detail: On these pages the step number is typeset within the cause text rather than its own cell, e.g. 'Defectiv pressure 6 voltage controlle' + 'e common rail sensor'. A straightforward table parser treats the row as a continuation of the previous step and drops it entirely.

Any pipeline that does not handle this will hand technicians a truncated procedure with no indication anything is missing.

title: Pages that are effectively invisible to text retrieval
detail: 220 pages carry under 250 characters of extractable text. 103 of those are dense vector graphics (circuit and hydraulic diagrams drawn as line art, not images).
impact: Text embeddings cannot represent these pages at all. Section 90 (Circuit Diagrams) is almost entirely in this category. They need page rasterisation plus a vision pass, or they will silently never be retrieved.

title: Codes with a troubleshooting page but absent from the Failure Code Table
detail: The reverse gap: a full procedure exists but the code is missing from the summary table used for lookup.
impact: Any lookup path that starts from the summary table will never reach these procedures.

title: Codes with no action level in either source
detail: Neither the summary table nor the detail page assigns an action level.
impact: The assistant cannot tell the technician whether the machine is safe to keep operating.

title: Detail page omits an action level the summary table assigns
detail: The summary table gives the code an action level; its own troubleshooting page leaves the field blank or prints a dash.
impact: A reader who goes straight to the code's page never learns how urgent it is.

title: Circular cross-reference chains
detail: Following the manual's own instructions leads back to the starting code.
impact: Hop-expansion and any automated 'follow the reference' logic must carry a visited set and a depth limit, or the assistant will loop forever.

title: Codes with no 'Phenomenon on machine' field
detail: The manual does not state what the operator will actually observe.
impact: The assistant cannot confirm it is working on the right problem, and cannot help a technician who describes a symptom rather than a code.

title: Format-A steps with an incomplete YES/NO branch
detail: Format-A codes are decision trees, so every step should offer both outcomes. Some do not, either in the manual or after table extraction.
impact: The executor has no defined next state when the missing branch is taken.

title: Different codes sharing an identical display name
detail: The text shown on the machine monitor is the same for several distinct codes with different procedures.
impact: A technician who reports only the screen text, not the code, cannot be disambiguated. The assistant must ask for the code itself.

title: The same printed page number appears on multiple pages
detail: Printed page numbers are not unique across the document.
impact: Citations that use only the printed page number are ambiguous. Every citation must carry the section code and the PDF page as well.

title: Monitoring codes referenced by troubleshooting procedures
detail: 54 distinct monitoring codes (e.g. 36500, 03203) are cited as the way to verify a reading, but the monitoring code table lives in a different part of the manual.
impact: Each of these is a required second hop. Without it the assistant tells the technician to 'check with the monitoring function' and stops there.

title: Pages carrying no printed page number
detail: Section dividers and full-bleed diagram pages have no footer.
impact: Content on these pages cannot be cited the way a technician expects.

title: Japanese CID fonts present in an English manual
detail: The document was produced from a Japanese source; CJK-encoded fonts remain in the file and poppler reports a missing Adobe-Japan1 mapping.
impact: Harmless for the English text layer, but some extraction tools emit encoding warnings or drop affected glyphs.

title: Document is AES encrypted with modification denied
detail: Permissions allow printing and copying but deny changes. Some libraries refuse to open it or silently return empty text.
impact: Normalise with `qpdf --decrypt` before the ingestion pipeline, or tool behaviour will vary across the fleet.

title: Criteria that are legitimately non-numeric
detail: Continuity checks and audible/visual confirmations have no numeric value by design.

title: Section sizes are extremely unbalanced
detail: Section 40 (Troubleshooting) is 956 pages, 43% of the manual; Section 90 (Circuit Diagrams) is 44 pages of almost pure graphics.
impact: A single chunking and embedding strategy applied uniformly will be wrong for most of the document. Section-specific parsing is required.
